html:
In June 860 a fleet of the Rus', Norse-led raiders from the lands that later became Kievan Rus', sailed down the Bosporus and attacked the suburbs of Constantinople. It was the first recorded clash between the Rus' and Byzantium.

The timing was well chosen. Emperor Michael III and the army were away fighting the Arabs in Anatolia, and the fleet was absent too. The raiders plundered the outskirts and the islands of the Sea of Marmara, killing many people. The patriarch Photios preached two sermons on the attack that survive, describing the city's terror. After some weeks the Rus' withdrew. How and why is unclear; later legend credited a robe of the Virgin dipped in the sea.

Soon after, Photios sent a bishop to the Rus', the first Byzantine attempt to convert them. Raids and trade took turns for the next century, from Oleg's raid and trade treaty in 907 to the baptism of Rus' in 988.
